subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint: deployment mode & PII handling (decision window)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint: deployment mode & PII handling (decision window)

Hi Jane / Acme team,

Per our MAP cadence I wanted to capture the current decision points so we have a clean close timeline this quarter. High-level asks for this week:

- Finalize deployment mode preference (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC vs On-prem light).
- Confirm retention windows for user-generated content and PII fields (examples below).
- Decide whether to require on-prem data ingress for filtered PII items.

Context / options we've outlined in the attached MAP:
1) Hosted (fastest path) — Redwood handles inference in our hosted fleet. We can offer configurable token retention (default 7 days, optional 0 days for redaction), and SOC2, but no customer-managed VPC.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — Data isolation with tenant-only pools, supports customer-managed KMS, 30/90/365-day retention profiles.
3) Private (VPC or on-prem) — Customer deploys a private control plane (VPC-peered or on-prem package). Full retention control and air-gap options; longer provisioning lead time (2–4 weeks).

PII examples we need answers on: name, email, payment token, full address, order ids. For each category, indicate: allowed for model input? stored in logs? retention days?

Proposed close timeline: decision by EOD Thu (Apr 15) to hit our ramp plan for May. If Acme chooses Private/VPC we will lock provisioning slots and begin onboarding next week.

Action items (proposed owners):
- Acme: provide retention matrix for PII categories — owner: Jane (due Wed Apr 14)
- Redwood SRE: outline minimal on-prem surface area and network requirements — owner: Monica (due Thu Apr 15)
- Redwood Legal: prepare clause for retention & log access — owner: Karthik (due Fri Apr 16)

Attached: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP with live timeline), soc2-data-retention-excerpt.pdf (relevant excerpt).

Quick note on risk: If you require <30d retention with hosted, we recommend Dedicated+DLP rules to avoid cross-tenant telemetry. If on-prem is required for any PII fields, we should flag that as a deployment gating item.

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync tomorrow to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Rishi

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we finalize:

1) For the Dedicated option, can we enforce zero-knowledge logs for payment tokens (we cannot store full tokens)?
2) If we choose VPC with Redwood private control plane, will model updates be managed by Redwood or will we be able to pin model versions ourselves?
3) Is there a way to scope only a subset of endpoints to on-prem (e.g., high PII endpoints on-prem, everything else hosted)?

We will try to get you a retention matrix tomorrow but procurement may push for procurement-specific timelines if Dedicated pricing needs review.

—Jane
Jane Doe
Sr. Product Security Manager, Acme Retail
jane.doe@acmeretail.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmeretail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint: deployment mode & PII handling (decision window)

Hi Jane — quick technical responses inline and a short recommendation.

1) Zero-knowledge logs for payment tokens: we can implement token hashing + truncation at ingestion for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we can provide a middleware redaction rule but cannot guarantee zero-knowledge unless you opt for Private on-prem or Dedicated with custom ingestion hooks.

2) Model pinning on VPC: the private control plane model management allows you to pin specific model versions; Redwood will propose updates and you can opt-in. For full autonomy on minor model retrains, the on-prem package is better.

3) Hybrid endpoint routing: yes — we support per-route routing policies. You can route traffic flagged with PII to a Private deployment or to a Dedicated pool that has stricter retention. This is common for customers who want minimal on-prem surface area.

Recommendation (to make decision window feasible):
- If Acme can provide a retention matrix by Wed Apr 14, we recommend selecting Dedicated with per-route routing to start. That gets you isolation and key management while limiting on-prem work. If procurement requires air-gap guarantees for tokens, plan for a Private on-prem pilot for the high-PII endpoints.

Action items (updated):
- Jane: retention matrix (due Wed Apr 14)
- Monica: minimal network/IP table + proposal for per-route routing config (due Thu Apr 15)
- Karthik: redline guidance and sample contract clause for token handling (due Fri Apr 16)

I attached a short checklist for the dedicated setup (see Acme_MAP_v2.pdf). Happy to run through the network table on Thursday.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

Thanks everyone — quick status and next steps to close the MAP this week.

Status:
- Jane: retention matrix received this morning (thanks) — confirms 3 categories: low-sensitivity (chat/text) 30d, medium (order history) 90d, high (payment tokens) 0d / hashed.
- Procurement: reviewing Dedicated pricing; flagged one payment-term question (procurement@acmeretail.com).
- Monica: network table ready; minimal on-prem footprint estimated as a single inference gateway + audit collector if you go hybrid.

Next steps to finalize by Fri EOD:
- Redwood Legal (Karthik) to send a one-page addendum covering token handling & retention (owner: Karthik) — due Apr 16 EOD.
- Procurement to confirm whether Dedicated pricing cadence is acceptable or if they require an on-prem pilot (owner: procurement@acmeretail.com) — requested by Apr 20.
- Redwood Ops (Monica) and Acme infra to schedule a 30-min network walkthrough (owner: Monica & Jane) — target: Mon Apr 19.

If we get the addendum approved, Redwood will provision a Dedicated pool scoped to Acme and prepare per-route routing rules to ensure high-PII traffic never leaves the dedicated/hashed path. That will keep most latency and cost benefits of hosted while meeting your token-handling requirement.

I'll prepare a short summary for the execs once the addendum is signed. Good progress — appreciate the fast turnaround on the retention matrix.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
